harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, cron scheduling is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (opsadmin user created since it didn't exist). Verified enforcement works (allowed for root/opsadmin, denied for other users) both before and after a full node restart, which was confirmed via a changed boot_id.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 cron setup: cronie installed, crond active, no /etc/cron.allow existed, /etc/cron.deny was empty (meaning all users were allowed)
Created missing opsadmin user with useradd -m
Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin'
Verified via sudo -u <user> crontab that opsadmin (and root) can schedule cron jobs while a disallowed test user is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and cron config state
Restarted node1 via 'systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified post-restart: crond active, /etc/cron.allow intact, opsadmin exists and can use crontab
Re-verified post-restart that a newly created non-listed user is still denied crontab access
Cleaned up all temporary test users (testuser, verifyuser)

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs on node1 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow (all users allowed) and no opsadmin user; created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root+opsadmin; confirmed opsadmin can use crontab and testuser is rejected with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'
Pre-restart boot_id 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d, crond active, /etc/cron.allow contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin user exists

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' with a short delay; exec returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, exit_code 0

evidence.requirement: Proof that node1's boot identity changed (actual restart occurred)
evidence.summary: boot_id was still 21972395-... shortly after triggering reboot, then changed to 32e4f377-96e0-4919-b987-37f776ee9ed2 once exec became available again, proving an actual kernel restart

evidence.requirement: Cron access-control config and service recovered after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart: crond active, /etc/cron.allow still contains root/opsadmin, opsadmin user intact, and opsadmin successfully installs a crontab entry

evidence.requirement: Restriction still enforced against non-listed users after restart
evidence.summary: Newly created verifyuser (not in cron.allow) was denied crontab access post-restart with the same 'not allowed to use this program' error; verifyuser subsequently removed

attempts.summary: On node1, cron scheduling is now restricted to root and opsadmin via /etc/cron.allow (opsadmin user created since it didn't exist). Verified enforcement works (allowed for root/opsadmin, denied for other users) both before and after a full node restart, which was confirmed via a changed boot_id.
